name: GoHighLevel

auth_methods: interactive HighLevel sign-in and consent (current hosted MCP; no PIT/API key required)
findings.api_type: REST; vendor-hosted operational MCP; separate Marketplace Developer MCP
findings.api_breadth: Broad agency/sub-account CRM and marketing resources. Current operational MCP supports contacts, conversations, calendars, invoices, promotions and workflows across approved sub-accounts; actions depend on permissions and enabled products.

evidence.title: HighLevel Private Integrations
evidence.excerpt: PITs are scoped static bearer tokens for API v2, generated by permitted agency admins; obsolete API v1 keys are a different route.

evidence.title: HighLevel OAuth 2.0
evidence.excerpt: OAuth apps configure scopes and client credentials; a location/agency admin installs and authorizes the integration.

evidence.title: HighLevel MCP Server
evidence.excerpt: Current hosted operational MCP uses HighLevel login and consent, needs no API/PIT key, and differs from the app-building Developer MCP.

evidence.title: HighLevel Pricing
evidence.excerpt: HighLevel advertises a self-service trial and paid subscriptions; Basic API access is listed under Unlimited.

notes: Independently read current first-party pages before viewing baseline. REST bearer-token setup must not be carried over to the current v2 operational MCP. Precise API entitlement can depend on plan and account role; no account or tool execution was tested.

name: systeme.io

auth_methods: X-MCP-Key header or mcpKey URL parameter (MCP)
findings.api_breadth: REST supports contacts, tags and broader documented marketing/commerce resources. MCP has confirmed common coverage for contacts, tags, contact fields and newsletters; newer help lists additional capabilities while older developer docs explicitly limit scope, so extended MCP coverage remains uncertain.

evidence.title: Systeme.io Public API
evidence.excerpt: The public API follows REST conventions, accepts only X-API-Key authentication, and documents shared rate limits and contact/tag operations.

evidence.title: Systeme.io MCP Server technical guide
evidence.excerpt: Initial-release MCP uses X-MCP-Key or mcpKey and lists contacts, tags, fields and newsletters as its only supported operations.

evidence.title: How to use the systeme.io MCP server
evidence.excerpt: The newer November 2026 help page lists broader MCP actions, limits keys to 90 days/two keys, and says OAuth is planned rather than supported.

evidence.title: Systeme.io Pricing
evidence.excerpt: A non-expiring free account is offered without a card; API/MCP key guides show account-setting generation without an explicit paid prerequisite.

notes: First-party docs disagree about MCP breadth: developer guide updated six months ago says contacts/newsletters only, while help updated November 10 lists campaigns, products, courses and other actions. Keep the common verified subset and validate the current tool catalogue before promising broader MCP coverage. Free product signup is documented; no free-account key issuance was executed.

name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud

auth_methods: Account Manager OAuth client credentials/token for SCAPI Admin APIs
SLAS OAuth 2.1 public/private clients for Shopper APIs
configured B2C instance credentials for local MCP; MRT API key/WebDAV credentials for relevant tooling
findings.api_breadth: B2C Shopper APIs cover browsing, cart and checkout; Admin APIs read/write product, order and inventory data. Official B2C MCP provides documentation search, live debugging/log investigation, deployment workflows and general SCAPI Admin API access under configured credentials.

evidence.title: Get Started with the B2C Commerce API
evidence.excerpt: SCAPI is REST and included for B2C customers; Shopper and Admin surfaces use separate auth, and a demo sandbox is distinct from an owned instance.

evidence.title: Authorization for SCAPI Admin APIs
evidence.excerpt: Administrators provision Account Manager API clients with instance roles and selected scopes; shopper scopes do not belong on Admin clients.

evidence.title: SLAS Overview
evidence.excerpt: Shopper APIs use SLAS public/private clients and OAuth2.1; SLAS administration requires an organization admin role.

evidence.title: Agentic B2C Developer Toolkit
evidence.excerpt: Salesforce provides B2C MCP with general SCAPI Admin access, debugging, logs and deployments; actions depend on configured credentials and scopes.

notes: Independent review is explicitly B2C Commerce. General Salesforce CRM MCP does not establish Commerce Cloud support. The official B2C tooling MCP is more than documentation search, but is not evidence of unrestricted shopper or B2B Commerce access. Demo examples do not grant full tenant credentials.

name: fanbasis

auth_methods: x-api-key from merchant/seller dashboard to create embedded checkout sessions
findings.api_type: HTTP/REST-style embedded checkout endpoint; JavaScript and React SDKs
findings.api_breadth: Verified public integration surface is embedded payment checkout/session creation plus checkout lifecycle, form, coupon, addon and event SDK methods. A broad seller administration API and current MCP were not established.

evidence.title: FanBasis Checkout Session Secret
evidence.excerpt: Rendered official docs show x-api-key on POST /public-api/checkout-sessions/embedded, merchant-dashboard keys and separate sandbox/production secrets.

evidence.title: FanBasis Payment SDK Getting Started
evidence.excerpt: A merchant account, creator/product identifiers and a session secret are prerequisites; the sandbox tests payments without real charges.

evidence.title: FanBasis Payment SDK API Reference
evidence.excerpt: The reference documents checkout SDK classes, configuration, fields, coupons, addons and events, rather than broad seller-resource CRUD or MCP.

notes: Official documentation was read through automated Chrome UI because HTTP extraction returned empty JavaScript shells. No signup or payment was submitted, no key was generated and no endpoint was executed. Merchant eligibility, API-key enablement, pricing and production approval remain unverified; merchant signup alone would not prove free API access. Searches on official domains did not establish a vendor MCP; this is not proof of absence.

name: Ahrefs

auth_methods: OAuth consent creating MCP-scoped key or manually generated MCP key (MCP)
findings.api_breadth: Broad SEO/data APIs cover Site Explorer, Keywords Explorer, SERP, Rank Tracker, Site Audit, Brand Radar and selected management operations. Hosted MCP exposes permitted Ahrefs data to supported AI tools; it is not a general-purpose API for scripts/bridges.

evidence.title: Ahrefs API v3 Introduction
evidence.excerpt: API v3 exposes SEO datasets and selected project/list management; eligible paid plans fund API units, while other plans have limited free test queries.

evidence.title: Ahrefs API key management
evidence.excerpt: REST requests use bearer API keys; workspace owners/admins generate and manage those keys.

evidence.title: About API v3
evidence.excerpt: Direct API, MCP and Ahrefs Connect share API limits and are available on Lite and higher subscriptions.

evidence.title: What is Ahrefs MCP
evidence.excerpt: Ahrefs hosts an OAuth/key MCP on Lite+ but explicitly prohibits using its external MCP via custom scripts, bridges or standalone HTTP/JSON-RPC clients, directing programmatic use to REST.

notes: Free fixed test queries do not establish general free production API access. A Composio-style direct connector should use the public REST API rather than repurpose the hosted MCP endpoint as an unrestricted backend bridge. No API calls were made.

name: MrScraper

auth_methods: Bearer API token for Marketplace endpoints
findings.api_type: REST; official hosted or self-managed MCP
findings.api_breadth: REST scraping, search, extraction and workflow resources. The directly read MCP v0.5.0 documents seven tools: status, scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, getScreenshot, scrapeBrand, scrapeJson and webSearch; broader workflow management is not established through MCP.

evidence.title: MrScraper API Overview
evidence.excerpt: MrScraper describes a REST API using JSON requests/responses for scraping and structured data.

evidence.title: MrScraper Authentication
evidence.excerpt: Users create dashboard API tokens; standard endpoints use x-api-token while Marketplace endpoints use Authorization Bearer.

evidence.title: MrScraper MCP Server
evidence.excerpt: Official MCP v0.5.0 exposes seven retrieval/search/status tools, hosted OAuth2.1 or key fallback, and published self-managed transports.

evidence.title: MrScraper Pricing
evidence.excerpt: A no-card Free plan and self-service dashboard API tokens are documented, with paid plans for greater usage.

notes: Directly opened MCP docs list v0.5.0/seven tools; search snippets still described v0.3.0/three tools and were not used as the current tool inventory. API key fallback carries full account authority; OAuth scopes are narrower. No credential or endpoint was tested.
